mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates a strong economy, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment below 6% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity prices.
failure_condition: Unemployment falls below 6% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production and housing starts indicate economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both industrial production and housing starts increase, but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate during tightening suggests lower equity valuations, leading to negative returns.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests accommodative monetary policy, boosting equity markets.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL growth is low but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth indicates economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Payroll growth exceeds 0.5% MoM but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and falling unemployment indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Retail sales rise and unemployment falls, but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment in late-cycle expansion signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Unemployment is low in late-cycle but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.
